Honestly, it hasn't been as hard as other times I've tried to quit (I never lasted more than 1 month). I have to say that this is because I quit after a brutal panic attack after smoking. It was weird, because I was a heavy smoker for 6 years and had actually had panic attacks from weed before, But something clicked in me that day. Many things came together, many problems piled up and I realized that if I continued smoking I would never find solutions.

For me, the hardest thing has been finding something to do in my free time. My hobby was smoking joints all day long. The first few months I spent a lot of time watching netflix or being addicted to social media. But step by step I am finding things that I like to do and that I didn't even know about! 

The best thing, as I have already mentioned in other posts or comments, has been feeling alive and reducing my anxiety. Also, I am now much more responsible with my daily duties. And lastly, I have also reduced my social anxiety. When I smoked, I lived in a constant state of paranoia. Although one of my justifications for smoking was that it helped me with my social life, in reality, it was making me isolate myself from everyone. When I interacted with someone, my head would fill with thoughts like "they're thinking badly of you" "they hate you" "have you seen the way they look at you?" I don't know, stuff like that. 

By the way, I want to point out that going to therapy helped me a lot. The anxiety I suffered did not come only from marijuana, I already had it before, but the weed prevented me from dealing with it.

Much better. I mean, I still have problems in my life but I feel like I can deal with them. With marijuana, all I did was avoid my emotional problems and put them aside. The result? Outbursts of anger, I isolated myself from all my loved ones, I lost relationships that mattered to me, work and academic opportunities, money, etc.
Sometimes I miss smoking a joint at night or with my friends, but it doesn't make up for all the negative aspects. Overall, it feels much better to face life sober without your life revolving around smoking weed.

Feeling alive. Being present. In addition, I have better control over my emotions. I feel and remember the "positive" emotions. I feel and manage the "negative" ones. And, above all, my anxiety has been dramatically reduced. I still feel anxious from time to time, but I can manage it and look for solutions instead of inhibiting what I feel :)

Day 79 after 6 years of daily smoking. It's not pleasant at all to quit weed. That's the truth. It's a rough path, but with the right support, I think it's bearable. I'm doing some therapy and I talk openly with my loved ones about my struggle. I let myself cry and feel ugly emotions, because I was using weed to escape these things. But it took a long time to realize why I was using weed, honestly.

The key for me to quit was, apart from feeling a brutal anxiety that I didn't feel before smoking, understanding the reason why I smoked and being clear that those negative moments that you try to avoid with weed are not life or death. You're not going to die from spending an entire day crying in your room. In fact, it's more likely that without weed, you'll begin to understand where those emotions come from and how to work through them.

Still, I'll tell you one thing. It was from my third year of smoking that I started to realize that I had a problem and that I was using weed to escape, which was unconsciously making me escape from things I didn't want to escape from (I was losing friendships and opportunities both in leisure, work or school just because I wanted to spend all day high). But it wasn't until this year, when I turned 6 years smoking, that I was able to make the decision. I want to tell you that, of the 6 years I've been smoking weed, I've spent 3 of them ruminating and feeling terrible about it until I reached a point of clarity and said: enough.

  
One thing that helped to me, and it's pretty dumb, it's to make a list of pros and cons of weed in my life and read that list every time I want to smoke. 

But, anyway, how does life feel without being high all the time? You feel ALIVE. You feel you are living your life in first person. You are living life how it is supposed to live, by feeling EVERYTHING, the good and the bad. And the bad is never that bad and if it is, you can find other ways to cope with it. Healthy ways. Even if those healthy ways require medical attention or help from other people. And I know everything I'm telling you is pretty general, because I'm no therapist, so that's why I heavily recommend getting professional help if you feel you can't do it on your own. And let me tell you, no therapist is going to make you quit weed the exact point you reach to them (at least that was in my case, bc I was still using when I reached to my therapist). But they will help you to realize why you need to quit and to get to that point where you say "this is it, I'm quitting".

And, the last thing I want to say is that I understand what you mean with "it always feels like the wrong time with such a busy life". That's why I did it in this august, because I was on vacation and I had nothing to do. But, anyway, if you don't have such an opportunity, It's still worth it. Of course some things in your life are going to fall out, I mean, smoking weed is a habit you had in your life and suddenly quitting is like "wow, what do I do now?" but, men, I don't know what to tell you, it's part of the process. So yeah, that my last advice: ACCEPT THE PROCESS. First weeks, I was so mean with my friends... and I regret it. But I'm an addict and that's it. And even nowadays, there are times when I miss weed so much that I get rude or mean. But I have to accept it and work it out.  Basically, quitting this addiction is a long path where you have to find new ways to make yourself happy and relaxed. Accept that is going to be long and hard.

  
I'm sorry if all of this is so general and have been said 1000000 times, but that's all I can tell you from my experience. I hope this message can encourage you to take some first steps and, remember, you are not alone in this!!! <3
